column1: # Win32-common reference pages admitted into corpus/win32/common/.
# The CE pages document the shared Win32 surface by name and meaning, but
# the base types carry no syntax block: "Windows Data Types" is one
# name|description table with the typedef body inside the row.  The
# MicrosoftDocs/win32 snapshot documents that shared surface in full
# (each row: the type, what it is, `typedef ...;`, and "This type is
# declared in WinNT.h").  Those pages are the Win32-common half of the
# corpus the CE books never printed as a reference page -- collected from
# Microsoft Learn's GitHub source (msdn/mslearn material), pinned like
# One row per admitted page.  tools/fetch-upstream.py common extracts them
# into corpus/win32/common/; tools/check-policy.py refuses anything under
# corpus/win32/common/ that this file does not name.  A page belongs here
# only when it documents the SHARED base surface: the types and the macros
# that stand for types, and the style/flag constant tables of the shared
# API surface (whose membership the CE-adapted w32api reference headers
# confirm -- sources/w32api-cegcc/) -- never a desktop-only feature area.

column2: path inside the pinned snapshot (see snapshot)
what the page documents, and why it is the shared surface
which pinned snapshot the member lives in (win32 = default;

column3: documents
Windows Data Types (BaseTsd.h): every base type with its typedef body and declaring header -- the shared Win32/CE type surface

#    corpus documents these NAMES (its Control Styles mother table, the
#    `Value | Description` flag lists) but rarely prints their numbers;
#    these reference pages print the name and value together, or list the
#    names beside their header (api_location).  The values land at the
#    marked `win32-reference`/shared rank: verify against the CE SDK.
